name: Medial approach to the calcaneus
corridor: Interval between the posterior tibial neurovascular bundle and flexor hallucis longus to the sustentaculum tali and medial calcaneal wall

positioning.text: Position supine with the hip externally rotated or use a bump so the medial hindfoot faces upward and remains accessible to imaging.

setup.text: Prep the leg and foot freely and confirm that lateral and axial heel fluoroscopic views can be obtained before incision.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the medial malleolus, navicular, sustentaculum tali, posterior tibial tendon, and anticipated course of the tarsal-tunnel neurovascular bundle.

incision.text: Place an approximately 5-cm incision parallel to the neurovascular bundle, centered inferior to the medial malleolus and directed toward the proximal navicular.

superficial_interval.text: Open flexor retinaculum and identify posterior tibial tendon, flexor digitorum longus, posterior tibial vessels and nerve, and flexor hallucis longus before developing a deep window.

deep_interval.text: Develop the interval between the posterior tibial neurovascular bundle and flexor hallucis longus, retracting FHL plantarly to expose sustentaculum and medial calcaneal wall.

layers.text: Skin and subcutaneous tissue, flexor retinaculum, identified tarsal-tunnel tendons and neurovascular bundle, interval beside FHL, then medial calcaneal periosteum and sustentaculum.

structures_encountered.text: Posterior tibial tendon, flexor digitorum longus, posterior tibial artery/veins and tibial nerve, flexor hallucis longus, sustentaculum tali, and deltoid-ligament fibers define the field.

structures_at_risk.text: The posterior tibial neurovascular bundle, medial calcaneal nerve branches, nerve to abductor digiti minimi, and flexor hallucis longus are at risk during exposure and fixation.

danger_zones.text: Do not create a blind window across the neurovascular bundle; identify every tarsal-tunnel structure and protect the bundle before working on either side of FHL.

retraction_hazards.text: Use gentle, intermittent retraction of the tibial neurovascular bundle and FHL and avoid fixed pressure within the confined tarsal tunnel.

exposure.text: Directly exposes the sustentaculum tali and medial/inferomedial calcaneal wall but does not provide the broad posterior-facet visualization of lateral approaches.

limitations.text: This is a targeted medial exposure for uncommon sustentacular or medial-wall pathology; most calcaneal fracture patterns are better addressed laterally or posteriorly.

extensions.text: Additional carefully separated windows may be developed around FHL and the protected bundle when fracture geometry requires more medial-wall access.

indications.text: Indicated for displaced sustentaculum-tali fractures, selected medial-wall reduction, and debridement of medial open calcaneal fractures.

relative_contraindications.text: Avoid using this limited corridor as the sole exposure when posterior-facet, lateral-wall, or calcaneal-body reduction cannot be verified medially.

implant_implications.text: Plan screw and plate trajectories around the tibial neurovascular bundle and FHL and confirm that fixation does not penetrate the subtalar joint.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use image intensification to localize the sustentaculum and verify reduction, screw trajectory, and avoidance of subtalar penetration.

closure.text: Release retractors and confirm neurovascular integrity, repair flexor retinaculum when appropriate, and close subcutaneous tissue and skin without tension.

complications.text: Complications include tibial or medial-calcaneal neuropathy, posterior tibial vascular injury, FHL injury or tethering, medial instability, wound problems, and intra-articular fixation.

bailouts.text: If neurovascular mobilization is unsafe or reduction cannot be assessed, stop blind medial work and add the fracture-appropriate lateral or posterior exposure.

procedure_applications.condition: A displaced sustentaculum-tali fragment or medial-wall target requires direct reduction
A medial open wound requires debridement and direct medial access

questions.question: What interval reaches the sustentaculum through the medial approach?
questions.answer: Between the posterior tibial neurovascular bundle and flexor hallucis longus.

questions.question: Which ligamentous fibers should be preserved to avoid medial instability and protect talar blood supply?
questions.answer: The tibiocalcaneal portion of the deltoid ligament.
